files.index_line: [Garden hose leak](garden-hose-leak.md) — far-spigot low pressure root cause = cracked brass Y-splitter (fixed 2026-05-30); check the splitter first, not the hose/regulator
files.body:
Far-bed low pressure at the far spigot is caused by a **cracked brass Y-splitter at that spigot** — confirmed and fixed 2026-05-30 by replacing the splitter. It is NOT the hose and NOT the pressure regulator.

**How to apply:** if far-bed pressure drops again, check the Y-splitter FIRST. Brass fittings on this property are age-failing (same mode hit sprinkler zone 3 — see [[sprinkler-timer]]), so treat any sudden pressure/flow loss as a fitting crack until proven otherwise.
changelog: 2026-04-02 first blamed a kinked hose (re-coiling changed nothing) — WRONG.
2026-04 swapped the pressure regulator — red herring, near-spigot pressure was always fine.
2026-05-30 root cause CONFIRMED: cracked brass Y-splitter; replacing it restored pressure.
Dead-ends, do not re-try: re-coil/replace hose, swap regulator, clean aerator screen.

files.index_line: [Sprinkler timer](sprinkler-timer.md) — zone 3 dry = cracked brass fitting (same mode as the hose); canonical note is garden-hose-leak
files.body:
Zone 3 ran dry because of a **cracked brass fitting at the zone-3 manifold** — the same age-failure mode as the far-spigot hose, not the timer program.

**How to apply:** the brass-fitting failure pattern is now tracked canonically in [[garden-hose-leak]]; treat sudden flow loss as a fitting crack until proven otherwise.
changelog: Initially reprogrammed the timer thinking the schedule was wrong — WRONG, schedule was fine.
Root cause = cracked brass manifold fitting; consolidated into [[garden-hose-leak]].
